title: Unrestricted offline ORAM bandwidth lower bounds
formal: Is logarithmic amortized bandwidth overhead necessary for offline oblivious RAM with constant client storage, even when stored words may be arbitrarily encoded rather than merely moved as indivisible items?
definitions: An offline simulation receives the logical read/write access sequence in advance and must hide that sequence through its physical memory-access distribution. Bandwidth overhead compares physical memory words transferred with logical operations. Constant client storage is measured in words. The question concerns unrestricted encoding of word contents. The precise word-size regime, sequence-length range, server storage, correctness and statistical-security conventions still require a completed source extraction; no universal bound across incompatible parameter regimes is asserted by this draft.

context_blocks.text: Oblivious memory is a central primitive for hiding access patterns. The historical logarithmic lower bound used a restriction on how data could be represented, and lifting that restriction in the offline setting exposes a connection to Boolean circuit lower bounds.

Later online lower bounds do not automatically apply when the whole logical access sequence is known beforehand. Moreover, online/offline separations with different logical and physical word sizes make the parameter choices consequential.

why: A major lower-bound barrier for oblivious computation, linking memory privacy to fundamental circuit complexity.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
